candidate.scope: The supplied Illumina ATAC-Seq schematic: native chromatin with exposed DNA is tagmented by adapter-loaded Tn5, then the tagged fragments undergo the depicted combined DNA purification/amplification block to yield a DNA library. The left assay-title icon and repeated Open DNA drawing describe the input; they do not depict a chromatin-opening operation. Blue Tn5 icons mark the reagent and its action. The insertion and fragmentation panels illustrate one tagmentation transformation. There is one route and no depicted alternative, compartment split, pooling or cell barcode. Fast-ATAC and other adaptations mentioned in catalogue text are not additional schematic targets.

operations.label: Insert in regions of open chromatin → Fragmented and primed
operations.description: Adapter-loaded Tn5 acts on exposed DNA within chromatin, simultaneously cleaving DNA and transferring adapter tags. The transposome-bearing insertion panel and the subsequent fragmented/primed panel show stages of this one local tagmentation event. DNA changes from continuous chromatin substrate to tagged fragments; this is not a separate adapter-ligation workflow.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 is the catalytic transposase carried in an adapter-loaded transposome. The adapters become associated with genomic fragment ends, whereas the blue enzyme is a processing reagent, not the DNA readout carrier.
operations.information_effect: The genomic sequence and insertion-defined fragment boundaries retain an association with DNA accessible to Tn5 at assay time. This is preferential sampling, not perfect biological selection for originally nucleosome-free DNA; the catalogue cautions that processing can expose previously bound chromatin.

operations.label: DNA purification / Amplification
operations.description: The shared DNA purification / Amplification block converts fragmented, adapter-tagged chromatin DNA into a purified, amplified DNA library. operations.mechanism: Amplification uses the adapter-derived priming interface on recoverable tagged fragments; the primary ATAC-Seq paper identifies PCR as the amplification step.

Paired-end lengths can additionally reflect nucleosome packing. No data-analysis step or single-cell identity is depicted.
